questions.q: What happens to a container that exceeds its --memory limit?
options: Docker automatically raises the limit to let it continue
The container is OOM-killed by the kernel, typically exiting with code 137
The container is paused until memory frees up elsewhere on the host
Nothing -- memory limits are advisory only and never enforced
questions.explain: A --memory limit is a hard cap. Exceeding it triggers the kernel's out-of-memory killer, which terminates the container, commonly surfaced as exit code 137.

questions.q: In docker run --cpus="0.5", what does 0.5 represent?
options: Half of one CPU core's worth of processing time
The container can only run for 0.5 seconds before being killed
Five hundred megabytes of memory
The container permanently runs at half its normal clock speed
questions.explain: --cpus caps the container to that fraction of one CPU core's worth of processing time on average.

questions.q: In a compose.yaml, which key sets a hard cap on CPU and memory a service can use?
options: deploy.resources.reservations
deploy.resources.limits
ports
healthcheck
questions.explain: deploy.resources.limits defines the hard ceiling a service's CPU and memory usage cannot exceed.

questions.q: What's the difference between deploy.resources.limits and deploy.resources.reservations?
options: limits is a hard maximum; reservations is a softer minimum Docker tries to guarantee
They are identical and can be used interchangeably
limits only applies to memory; reservations only applies to CPU
reservations caps usage while limits reserves capacity
questions.explain: limits caps the maximum a service can use; reservations is a softer guarantee of a minimum amount of resources being available to it.

questions.q: Why does setting resource limits matter once Northbridge runs multiple containers on one host?
options: It's required before any container can start at all
It prevents one runaway or leaking container from starving CPU or memory from every other container sharing that host
It automatically distributes containers across multiple physical servers
It encrypts network traffic between containers
questions.explain: Resource limits keep one misbehaving container from consuming all of a shared host's CPU or memory and taking the others down with it.
